questions.question: Which of the following states has the lowest female literacy rate as per Census of India 2011?

questions.question: Which is the oldest and most widespread industry in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Textile**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Textile industry** is the **oldest **and most widespread **industry **in India.
 
• It plays a significant role in the Indian economy by providing employment to millions and contributing substantially to the country's export earnings.
 
• The industry covers a wide range of activities from the production of raw materials like cotton, jute, silk, and wool, to the manufacturing of finished products like garments and apparels.
 
• India has a rich heritage of textiles, with a history that dates back to ancient times, when Indian textiles were highly sought after in international markets.
 
• The industry is known for its diverse range of products, including traditional handloom and handicraft items, as well as modern, machine-made fabrics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indian textile industry** is one of the largest in the world, with a vast raw material base and manufacturing strength across the value chain.
 
• The industry contributes around **7% to India's industrial output** in value terms, **2% to the GDP, and 15% to the country's export earnings**.
 
• It is the second largest employer in the country after agriculture, employing over 45 million people directly and 60 million people indirectly.
 
• Government initiatives like the **Textile Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS)** and **Make in India** campaign have provided a significant boost to the sector.
 
• The sector is expected to reach **USD 300 billion by 2025** with a CAGR of 10%.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs is/are INCORRECTLY matched?

A. Separation of Executive from the Judiciary – Article 50

B. Organisation of the village panchayats and endow them with powers – Article 40

C. Promote justice, on a basis of equal opportunity, and to provide free legal aid to the poor – Article 39A

D. Organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines – Article 45
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**D only**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 50** deals with the Separation of Executive from the Judiciary.
 
• **Article 40** pertains to the Organisation of village panchayats and endows them with powers.
 
• **Article 39A** promotes justice on a basis of equal opportunity and provides free legal aid to the poor.
 
• **Article 45** originally dealt with the provision for free and compulsory education for children. However, it was amended, and the provision for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years was added.
 
• Therefore, the statement "Organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines" does not belong to Article 45, making it incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **directive to organize agriculture and animal husbandry** on modern and scientific lines is actually found in **Article 48** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The directive principles of state policy aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They also aim to establish social and economic democracy through a welfare state.
 
• While these principles are** non-justiciable**, they are fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

questions.question: When is the Constitution Day observed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**26 November**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Constitution Day**, also known as **Samvidhan Divas**, is observed on **26th November** every year in India.
 
• It commemorates the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949**.
